hints: XOR combinations form a vector space over bits.
Build a basis with at most one pivot for each highest set bit.
Greedily XOR basis vectors from high pivot to low when that increases the answer.
analogy: A basis is a small toolbox from which every obtainable XOR can be assembled.
example: For [1,6,12], choosing 1 and 12 gives 13, the maximum subset XOR.
algorithm: Insert each value into an XOR basis: eliminate its highest set bit using an existing vector, or store it as the vector for that pivot if none exists. Starting from zero, inspect basis vectors from highest pivot downward and XOR a vector whenever the result increases.
correctness: Elimination preserves the set of representable XORs. At each pivot, setting that highest undecided bit improves the number more than any lower bits can offset; greedy choices therefore give the maximum.
complexity: For n values and B bits, O(nB+B^2) time and O(B) space.
